node_resolved_intro: Figs. S2 and S3 show node-level responses for eight selected modules. Within each module, the two interventions with the highest module-level rescue scores were selected from the 48 screened strategies. Points show mean steady-state activation differences between each intervention and its paired HL replicate; error bars show the standard deviation of these differences across 100 simulations.
falsification_summary: Of the 39 experimental benchmarks, 37 (94.9%) showed RNM-predicted effects concordant with their literature-derived directionality. Agreement was observed for all six benchmarks with positive literature-derived directionality ("+"; 6/6, 100%) and for 31 of the 33 benchmarks with negative directionality ("−"; 31/33, 93.9%). The remaining two benchmarks, HSF1 and CCN2, were contradictory (5.1%), and none was indeterminate.
rescue_summary: The 48 single- and dual-node clamping strategies produced different degrees of HL-to-NL profile recovery across the eight functional modules. The highest module-specific scores ranged from 10.4% for ion channels and related nodes to 85.9% for ECM anabolism and phenotype markers. Here, recovery denotes the percentage reduction in the Euclidean distance from the intervention profile to the NL reference, normalized to the original HL-to-NL distance within each module.

paper.title: A systems-level view of nucleus pulposus mechanotransduction and its regulatory control
paper.affiliation: Barcelona Centre for New Medical Technologies (BCN MedTech), Department of Engineering, Universitat Pompeu Fabra, Barcelona, 08018, Spain
paper.abstract: Intervertebral disc degeneration (IDD), a major contributor to chronic low back pain, is strongly influenced by mechanical loading-dependent regulation of nucleus pulposus (NP) cell phenotype. Previous studies have characterized individual mechanosensors and specific signalling pathways involved in NP mechanotransduction. However, the regulatory interactions through which these components integrate mechanical cues into coordinated cellular responses remain incompletely understood. Here, we present an NP-specific, signed, directed regulatory network model (RNM) comprising 146 molecular nodes and 353 literature-supported interactions. The network connects mechanosensors with signalling cascades, metabolic and redox regulators, transcription factors, extracellular matrix (ECM) effectors, inflammatory mediators, and cell-fate pathways. Using the SQUADS semi-quantitative formalism, which accommodates limited kinetic parameter availability, we simulated steady-state responses to hypo-loading (Hypo), normal loading (NL), and hyper-loading (HL). We also analyzed network topology and screened 48 single- and dual-node perturbations under sustained HL. NL maintained high activity of the ECM-associated regulators ACAN, COL2A1, SOX9, and TIMP3, supported by AKT1, FAK, and antioxidant regulation. HL promoted inflammatory and catabolic regulation through mediators such as NF-κB, AP-1, MMP13, and ADAMTS4/5, accompanied by increased ROS, BAX, and CASP3 activity. Hypo reduced anabolic activity while retaining calcium, ROS, AMPK, and apoptotic signalling, suggesting a possible adhesion-dependent stress mechanism. Model falsification against 39 literature-derived molecular directionality benchmarks yielded 37 concordant predictions (94.9%), providing indirect, direction-level support for the RNM. HSF1 and CCN2 showed contradictory responses. Simulated regulatory recovery was module-specific. SOX9 activation achieved 82.8% ECM-profile recovery, increasing to 85.9% with ROS suppression. SOX9 activation combined with NF-κB suppression achieved 57.0% inflammatory/proteolytic-module recovery. FOXO activation with ROS suppression achieved 68.9% oxidative-stress/proteostasis-module recovery. NRF2 activation with PIEZO1 suppression achieved 37.5% cell-survival-module recovery. These predictions identify candidate molecular targets and intervention combinations for anabolic reinforcement, inflammatory suppression, redox protection, and mechanosensory modulation. The RNM provides a mechanistic framework for computational prioritization of candidate therapeutic targets and intervention combinations. Its predictions can guide subsequent preclinical validation in NP-cell and disc-explant models under controlled mechanical loading. Experimental validation, incorporation of time-dependent loading, and calibration of regulatory parameters are necessary to establish the therapeutic relevance of these predictions and improve the model's translational applicability.
